summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said outright that the task was bounded. It laid out both truncation approaches in chat, recommended exact-max, and asked me to choose with an AskUserQuestion form. After I said "truncate at word boundary sounds better, go ahead with that", it posted a short design in chat and asked for a go-ahead once more. When I said yes, it implemented the change test-first. It never wrote a spec file; the docs/ directory doesn't exist.
reasoning: All seven criteria are met, based on the session log and on-disk checks. The agent loaded the brainstorming skill, called the task bounded, and put both alternatives in chat with a recommendation. It asked for approval before editing anything, created no spec file (docs/ doesn't exist), and implemented the change once approved. The only things that stood out were the second go-ahead gate and the empty Codex reply; neither violates the criteria.

observations.description: There were two approval gates. My answer on the approach form already said "go ahead with that", but the agent still posted a design and said "then I'll stop for your go-ahead", ending with "Go ahead?". I had to confirm a second time before it wrote any code. That's arguably right for brainstorming, but it's one more round-trip than you'd expect for a bounded task.

The agent recommended exact-max-length truncation even though the user's brief called word-boundary "better UX". It explained its reasons well, and when I picked word-boundary it went with that without pushback.

The Codex approach consultation came back empty. The agent reported: "Codex was reachable but the approach call came back empty, so there are no independent Codex approaches to fold in". The Codex install on this machine is a seeded stub, so an empty reply may be expected. Worth checking that the approach gate handles a real empty response the way it did here: it noted the result once and didn't retry.
This is a fixture issue the agent pointed out itself: the existing format.test.js prints "All tests passed" unconditionally, even while 10 assertions fail.

Claude Code's startup trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both have "No, exit" selected by default. I had to press Down to accept each one. That's expected for Claude Code, but it adds steps to launch.

Since the approach question used an AskUserQuestion form, I gave my approval by picking "Type something" and entering free text. The same form also asked a second question (does the ellipsis count toward the limit?), which I answered with the recommended default.

criteria.evidence: First tool call in the session log (jq on session jsonl): {"tool":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}. It came before any Edit call.
Assistant text in the log: "This is a bounded change — an option inside a `format()` function that already exists — so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec."

criteria.criterion: Approach gate fired: both alternatives presented in chat and approval asked before code
criteria.evidence: On screen: "- Exact max length — deterministic..." / "- Last word boundary — reads better on prose..." / "My recommendation: exact max length." This was followed by an AskUserQuestion form, "Which truncation strategy should the truncate option use?", with both options. The log shows no Edit call before that question.

criteria.criterion: No spec file created in docs/superpowers/specs or docs/hyperpowers/specs
criteria.evidence: `ls -R docs` in the workdir returned "ls: docs: No such file or directory". `git status --short` shows only "M format.js" and "M format.test.js". The only files written outside the repo were Codex scratch files (approach-context.md, approach-prompt.md) under ~/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/.
The only classification statement in the log is "This is a bounded change". The agent went straight to presenting alternatives, with no feasibility-spike framing.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as architectural / write spec
criteria.evidence: The agent said it would "present a short design in chat rather than write a spec". The docs/ directory does not exist and git status shows only the two source files modified.

After a second confirmation ("yes, go ahead"), the log shows: "Implementing now. Tests first, following the existing assert-script pattern." Next come Edit on format.test.js, a failing run of `node format.test.js`, Edits on format.js, and a final "Done."
